title: collinear_trans: Collinearity Transitivity
content:
`theorem collinear_trans {p q r s : ℝ × ℝ} (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpqr : collinear p q r) (hpqs : collinear p q s) : collinear p r s`

Proof: Case split on `q.1 - p.1 = 0` (vertical line):
- **Vertical**: q.1 = p.1 forces r.1 = p.1 and s.1 = p.1 (by `mul_eq_zero`), so collinear p r s by ring.
- **Non-vertical**: multiply both sides of the collinearity equations, factor out (q.1 - p.1) ≠ 0, cancel via `mul_left_cancel₀`.

Key: `collinear_any_triple` uses this to prove transitivity for arbitrary triples on the same line.
mathContext: Collinearity transitivity: if $p, q, r$ and $p, q, s$ are collinear with $p \neq q$, then $p, r, s$ are collinear (all three lie on the unique line through $p$ and $q$). The signed-area definition requires a case split on whether the line is vertical, since the slope is undefined for vertical lines.

title: noFiveCollinear_line_bound: At Most 4 Points per Line
content:
`theorem noFiveCollinear_line_bound (P : PlanarPointSet) (hP : NoFiveCollinear P) (a b : ℝ × ℝ) (ha : a ∈ P.points) (hb : b ∈ P.points) (hab : a ≠ b) : (P.points.filter (fun p => collinear a b p)).card ≤ 4`

Proof: By contradiction. Let L = {p ∈ P | collinear a b p} and suppose |L| ≥ 5. Since a, b ∈ L, let L' = L.erase a, L'' = L'.erase b. Then |L''| ≥ 3.

Extract 3 distinct points c, d, e from L'' by `Finset.card_pos` + `obtain`. These 5 points a,b,c,d,e ∈ P.points are all collinear and pairwise distinct — contradicting `NoFiveCollinear P`.

The extraction uses repeated `Finset.mem_erase` to verify all distinctness hypotheses.
mathContext: The no-five-collinear condition forces every line to contain at most 4 points of $P$. This is the key constraint that makes the upper bound argument work: if lines could contain more points, a single 5-point collinear set would give infinitely many near-linear configurations.

title: four_collinear_overlap_small: Distinct 4-Subsets Share ≤1 Point
content:
`theorem four_collinear_overlap_small (P : PlanarPointSet) (hP : NoFiveCollinear P) (S₁ S₂ : ...) (hne : S₁ ≠ S₂) ... : (S₁ ∩ S₂).card ≤ 1`

Proof: By contradiction. If |S₁ ∩ S₂| ≥ 2, extract two shared points x, y ∈ S₁ ∩ S₂ with x ≠ y.

Since x, y ∈ S₁ and S₁ is collinear, all of S₁ lies on line(x,y). Similarly all of S₂ lies on line(x,y).

By `four_collinear_unique` (both S₁ and S₂ are the unique 4-subset on line(x,y)), S₁ = S₂ — contradicting hne.

This is the structural heart of the pair-packing argument.
mathContext: Two distinct four-point lines can share at most one point. If they shared two points $x, y$, both lines would be the line through $x$ and $y$, making them identical — contradiction. This is the combinatorial key enabling the packing argument.

title: improved_upper_bound: fourPointLineCount ≤ n(n-1)/12
content:
`theorem improved_upper_bound (P : PlanarPointSet) (hP : NoFiveCollinear P) : fourPointLineCount P ≤ P.points.card * (P.points.card - 1) / 12`

Proof: Let F be the family of 4-collinear subsets. Map each S ∈ F to its 6 pairs (pairSet S = S.powersetCard 2).

1. `hpair_card`: each pairSet has card = C(4,2) = 6 (by Finset.card_powersetCard + decide)
2. `hpair_disj`: distinct 4-subsets have disjoint pair-sets (from four_collinear_overlap_small + powersetCard2_disjoint)
3. `hbU_card`: |F.biUnion pairSet| = ∑_{S∈F} 6 = 6|F| (by Finset.card_biUnion on disjoint sets)
4. `hbU_le`: biUnion ⊆ P.points.powersetCard 2 of size n.choose 2 = n(n-1)/2
5. Combine: 6|F| ≤ n(n-1)/2 → |F| ≤ n(n-1)/12
mathContext: The pair-packing argument: each of the $|F|$ four-point lines contributes $\binom{4}{2}=6$ pairs of points. Since distinct four-point lines share at most 1 point, their pair-sets are disjoint. Packing into $\binom{n}{2}$ total pairs gives $6|F| \leq \binom{n}{2} = n(n-1)/2$, so $|F| \leq n(n-1)/12$.

title: fourCollinearThrough_bound: At Most (n-1)/3 Four-Point Lines Through One Point
content:
`theorem fourCollinearThrough_bound (P : PlanarPointSet) (hP : NoFiveCollinear P) (p : ℝ × ℝ) (hp : p ∈ P.points) : (fourCollinearThrough P p).card ≤ (P.points.card - 1) / 3`

Let FP = fourCollinearThrough P p. Map each S ∈ FP to S.erase p (3-element subset of P.points.erase p).

1. Each eraseMap S has card 3 (from |S|=4, p∈S, Finset.card_erase_of_mem)
2. eraseMap S ⊆ P.points.erase p (from S ⊆ P.points, p ∉ eraseMap S)
3. eraseMap is injective: S = (eraseMap S) ∪ {p} for S ∈ FP
4. eraseMap images are pairwise disjoint (from four_collinear_overlap_small: distinct S₁, S₂ ∈ FP share only p)
5. Packing: 3|FP| ≤ |P.points.erase p| = n-1, so |FP| ≤ (n-1)/3
mathContext: The per-point bound: at most $(n-1)/3$ four-point lines pass through any fixed point $p$. The key: erase $p$ from each four-point line through $p$ to get a 3-element set. By the overlap lemma, distinct four-point lines through $p$ share only $p$, so these 3-element sets are pairwise disjoint within $P \setminus \{p\}$ (of size $n-1$), giving the $n-1 \geq 3|F_p|$ packing.
